title: Keysight Collaborates with the Centre for Assuring Autonomy at the University of York to Advance AI Safety Assurance for Software-Defined Vehicles
content:
Research initiative aims to close gap between AI safety research and practical engineering to reduce risk and enable faster, safer deployment of AI-enabled automotive systems

SANTA ROSA, Calif., September 03, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) and the Centre for Assuring Autonomy (CfAA) at the University of York (UK) announced a research collaboration to advance the safe deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) in software-defined vehicles (SDVs). The collaboration will focus on developing practical methods for validating AI systems and generating the evidence needed to demonstrate their safety and reliability. The work is designed to enable automakers and suppliers to meet emerging industry requirements while reducing development risk and accelerating the deployment of AI-enabled automotive systems.

Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming a core technology in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), automated driving functions, and SDVs. As these capabilities become more sophisticated, automotive organizations face growing pressure to demonstrate that AI systems operate safely, reliably, and as intended, not only during development but throughout the vehicle lifecycle. Providing that proof is one of the industry's most significant challenges as automakers work to bring increasingly intelligent vehicles to market while meeting evolving regulatory and safety expectations.

Together, Keysight and the CfAA will help bridge the gap between AI safety research and practical engineering by advancing methodologies for structured AI safety cases and building justified confidence in the safety of AI-enabled automotive systems.

The research will focus on the creation of evidence-driven approaches to support the implementation of ISO/PAS 8800 requirements, exploring measurable safety-scoring methodologies grounded in academic research and industry standards, and creating practical frameworks for generating auditable AI safety evidence. The resulting methodologies are intended to support the process of building AI safety cases, improve confidence in AI validation, and help engineering teams demonstrate justified AI safety more efficiently throughout the product lifecycle.

The University of York is internationally recognized for its research in safety engineering, and the assurance of complex systems across domains, including transport and automotive. By combining the university's academic expertise with Keysight's AI validation techniques, the collaboration seeks to advance methodologies applicable to automotive AI development.

Story Continues

Simon Burton, Chair in Systems Safety, University of York, said: "The automotive industry is at a pivotal point where AI technologies are becoming increasingly integral to vehicle functionality. Ensuring these systems can be evaluated using robust, evidence-based approaches is essential. This is where the CfAA is ideally placed to support Keysight. We have produced several freely accessible frameworks and guidance already being used by industry safety professionals in the transport sector. This collaboration is another way we are supporting the advancement of practice methods that help translate AI safety principles into engineering practices that can be applied in safety-critical environments."

Lukas Klose, Head of the Automotive AI Solution Center, Keysight, said: "Automotive organizations need practical and scalable ways to build confidence in AI-enabled systems. By combining leading research in safety assurance with Keysight's holistic AI Validation Framework, we aim to develop methodologies that help engineering teams generate structured evidence for AI safety cases and support the deployment of trustworthy AI technologies in conformance with international standards such as ISO/PAS 8800."

The research is expected to inform future development of Keysight's AI Software Integrity Builder, enable enhanced support for AI safety arguments, safety evidence generation, and validation activities aligned with automotive industry expectations.

title: Wall Street Analysts Predict a 30% Upside in Keysight (KEYS): Here's  What You Should Know
content:
Shares of Keysight (KEYS) have gained 8.5% over the past four weeks to close the last trading session at $321.87, but there could still be a solid upside left in the stock if short-term price targets of Wall Street analysts are any indication. Going by the price targets, the mean estimate of $418.42 indicates a potential upside of 30%.

The mean estimate comprises 12 short-term price targets with a standard deviation of $19.48. While the lowest estimate of $390.00 indicates a 21.2% increase from the current price level, the most optimistic analyst expects the stock to surge 40.4% to reach $452.00. It's very important to note the standard deviation here, as it helps understand the variability of the estimates. The smaller the standard deviation, the greater the agreement among analysts.

While the consensus price target is a much-coveted metric for investors, solely banking on this metric to make an investment decision may not be wise at all. That's because the ability and unbiasedness of analysts in setting price targets have long been questionable.

But, for KEYS, an impressive average price target is not the only indicator of a potential upside. Strong agreement among analysts about the company's ability to report better earnings than they predicted earlier strengthens this view. While a positive trend in earnings estimate revisions doesn't gauge how much a stock could gain, it has proven to be powerful in predicting an upside.

Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseZacks Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise Chart for KEYS

Here's What You Should Know About Analysts' Price Targets

According to researchers at several universities across the globe, a price target is one of many pieces of information about a stock that misleads investors far more often than it guides. In fact, empirical research shows that price targets set by several analysts, irrespective of the extent of agreement, rarely indicate where the price of a stock could actually be heading.

While Wall Street analysts have deep knowledge of a company's fundamentals and the sensitivity of its business to economic and industry issues, many of them tend to set overly optimistic price targets. Are you wondering why?

They usually do that to drum up interest in shares of companies that their firms either have existing business relationships with or are looking to be associated with. In other words, business incentives of firms covering a stock often result in inflated price targets set by analysts.

However, a tight clustering of price targets, which is represented by a low standard deviation, indicates that analysts have a high degree of agreement about the direction and magnitude of a stock's price movement. While that doesn't necessarily mean the stock will hit the average price target, it could be a good starting point for further research aimed at identifying the potential fundamental driving forces.

Story Continues

That said, while investors should not entirely ignore price targets, making an investment decision solely based on them could lead to disappointing ROI. So, price targets should always be treated with a high degree of skepticism.

Why KEYS Could Witness a Solid Upside

Analysts' growing optimism over the company's earnings prospects, as indicated by strong agreement among them in revising EPS estimates higher, could be a legitimate reason to expect an upside in the stock. That's because empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

Over the last 30 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current year has increased 11%, as three estimates have moved higher compared to no negative revision.

Moreover, KEYS currently has a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), which means it is in the top 5% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on four factors related to earnings estimates. Given an impressive externally-audited track record, this is a more conclusive indication of the stock's potential upside in the near term. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Therefore, while the consensus price target may not be a reliable indicator of how much KEYS could gain, the direction of price movement it implies does appear to be a good guide.

title: Keysight’s (KEYS) Orders Just Topped $2B Again, But Can Supply Keep Up
content:
On August 18, Keysight Technologies (NYSE:KEYS) delivered a fiscal third quarter that beat the high end of its own guidance across the board. Revenue climbed 36% year over year to $1.85 billion, non-GAAP earnings per share jumped 79% to $3.07, and orders topped $2 billion for the second straight quarter. Management raised its outlook for both the fourth quarter and the full fiscal year, pointing to demand tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure, defense modernization, and next-generation communications standards. The results position Keysight as one of the more direct ways to invest in the testing and validation side of the AI buildout, a corner of the market most investors rarely think about.Keysight's (KEYS) Orders Just Topped $2B Again, But Can Supply Keep Up

Orders Piling Up Everywhere

Orders reached $2.091 billion in the quarter, up 56% on a reported basis, the second straight quarter above the $2 billion mark. Wireline orders more than doubled year over year as customers scaled out AI data center infrastructure, and Commercial Communications crossed $1 billion in quarterly revenue for the first time, up 56%, while revenue from wireline products outpaced wireless within that segment for the first time. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group posted a record $501 million in revenue, up 21%, with double-digit order growth across general electronics, semiconductors, and automotive and energy. Aerospace, defense and government revenue grew 14% to $339 million as spending shifted toward lower-cost autonomous platforms, including UAVs and low earth orbit satellite constellations built by venture-funded defense technology firms.

Profitability expanded right alongside the growth: operating margin hit 33.2%, up 820 basis points and above the company's long-term target range of 31% to 32%, while free cash flow rose to $403 million from $291 million a year earlier. The company also added nearly 3,000 new customers so far this fiscal year, a group that has already contributed more than $100 million in new business, and said July was its busiest month yet for incoming sales opportunities, pushing the trailing 12-month pipeline to a record. Further out, the 3GPP standards body confirmed in June that the first 6G standard is targeted for March 2029, a milestone management said is already moving customers from exploratory research into funded development work.

Supply Chains Set The Pace

CFO Neil Dougherty tempered the enthusiasm, warning that supply availability remains "a governor of our ability to convert demand into revenue" over the next several quarters, meaning orders are outrunning what the company can actually ship and book as revenue right now. He also noted that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 inflated this year's profitability in ways that are not expected to repeat in fiscal 2027. That combination, a backlog constrained by supply and a margin base partly lifted by tariffs, complicates how much of this quarter's strength carries forward unchanged. The integration of recent acquisitions is also still working through the system.

Story Continues

Keysight expects to realize 80% to 90% of its targeted $100 million in cost synergies on a run-rate basis by fiscal year-end, a quarter ahead of schedule, which is welcome but also a reminder that part of the current margin expansion is coming from cost cutting rather than pure operating leverage. Hyperscaler customers account for roughly 10% of Keysight's business directly, and while management described meaningful downstream influence across the broader ecosystem, that concentration ties results more tightly to a small group of AI infrastructure spenders than the diversified growth story suggests on the surface.

Wall Street's Read On It

The number of hedge funds holding Keysight rose from 66 to 71 quarter over quarter, pointing to institutions adding to positions rather than trimming them. Short interest sits at just 1.98% of the float, a level that shows little organized skepticism toward the stock. Keysight trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 20.33 as of August 26, a modest multiple given the growth rate management just reported and guided toward for the fourth quarter.

What Happens Next Matters

Keysight's fiscal third quarter left little doubt that demand tied to AI infrastructure, defense modernization, and next-generation communications is broad-based, with orders, revenue, and margins all landing ahead of guidance. Tellingly, the caution came from the company's own executives, who flagged supply constraints and a tariff-driven profitability boost unlikely to repeat next year.

While we acknowledge the potential of KEYS as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. title: Keysight Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Revenues Up Y/Y on Solid Demand
content:
Keysight Technologies, Inc. KEYS reported solid third-quarter fiscal 2026 results, with both top and bottom lines surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate.

The leading electronic design and testing solutions provider reported a 36% year-over-year increase in revenues, supported by broad-based demand across its key end markets and continued customer investments in emerging technologies. Artificial Intelligence (AI) infrastructure, next-generation connectivity and increasing adoption of advanced technologies continued to boost the company's performance.

Net Income

Net income on a GAAP basis was $397 million or $2.30 per share compared with $191 million or $1.10 per share in the prior-year quarter. Strong top-line growth boosted the bottom line during the quarter. 

Non-GAAP net income in the reported quarter was $531 million or $3.07 per share compared with $297 million or $1.72 per share in the prior-year quarter. The bottom line comfortably surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.46.

Keysight Technologies Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS SurpriseKeysight Technologies Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Keysight Technologies Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Keysight Technologies Inc. Quote

Revenues

Net sales during the quarter increased to $1.85 billion from $1.35 billion in the year-ago quarter. owing to healthy growth in both the Communication Solutions Group (CSG) and Electronic Industrial Solutions Group (EISG) segments. The top line beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.75 billion. Total orders were $2.09 billion compared with $1.34 billion in the year-ago quarter.

CSG generated $1.35 billion in revenues, up from the year-ago quarter's $940 million. The 43% year-over-year increase was driven by strong performance in wireline and wireless, as well as continued momentum in AI infrastructure and aerospace, defense and government. Emerging 6G and non-terrestrial network opportunities also supported demand. 

EISG segment's revenues increased to $501 million from $412 million in the prior-year quarter, driven by AI-related investments and capacity expansion in advanced semiconductors, along with solid demand for software-defined vehicles, cybersecurity and EV charging solutions. 

Region-wise, Asia-Pacific revenues aggregated $810 million compared with $569 million in the prior-year quarter. The company reported a 29% year-over-year improvement in revenues from the Americas to $729 million. Revenues from Europe were $307 million, up 41% from the year-ago quarter's $217 million.

During the quarter, revenues from Aerospace, Defense and Government increased to $339 million from $296 million in the year-ago quarter. The company reported a 56% year-over-year improvement in revenues from Commercial Communications to $1.01 billion. Electronic Industrial generated $501 million in revenues, up from the year-ago quarter's $412 million.

Story Continues

Other Details

During the quarter, the company's non-GAAP gross profit totaled $1.27 billion, up from $864 million in the year-ago quarter, with respective gross margins of 69% and 63.9%. Non-GAAP operating income totaled $614 million compared with $338 million in the year-ago period, with operating margins of 34.7% and 25%, respectively. 

CSG reported a non-GAAP operating income of $458 million compared with $246 million in the year-ago period. EISG non-GAAP operating income increased to $155 million from $92 million in the prior-year quarter.

Cash Flow & Liquidity

In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Keysight generated $437 million of net cash from operating activities compared with $322 million in the year-ago quarter. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026, the company generated $1.38 billion in cash compared with $1.18 billion in the year-ago period.  As of July 31, 2026, the company had $2.61 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $1.82 billion of long-term debt.

Outlook

For the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, Keysight expects revenues in the range of $1.93-$1.95 billion. Non-GAAP earnings per share are estimated to be between $3.34 and $3.40.

KEYS's Zacks Rank

Keysight currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

Other Stocks to Consider

Silicon Motion Technology Corporation SIMO sports a Zacks Rank #1 at present. In the last reported quarter, it delivered an earnings surprise of 14.08%. 

It is benefiting from growing demand for NAND flash storage solutions driven by AI, data centers, PCs, smartphones and automotive applications. Its focus on advanced controller technologies, PCIe Gen5 solutions and expanding embedded storage offerings is expected to support long-term growth and strengthen its position in the storage semiconductor market.

The company is experiencing strong demand for analog and embedded processing solutions across industrial, automotive, communications and personal electronics markets. Its focus on product innovation, manufacturing capacity expansion and embedded processing technologies is likely to drive long-term growth.

Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN carries a Zacks Rank #2 at present. It delivered an earnings surprise of 2.73% in the last reported quarter.

Amazon continues to gain from strong demand for e-commerce, cloud computing, and digital advertising services, supported by the growing adoption of AI. Its expanding Amazon Web Services business, investments in generative AI and cloud infrastructure, and growing fulfillment network support sustained growth and strengthen its competitive position.

title: Keysight Technologies, Inc. Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Keysight Technologies, Inc. Q3 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers

Performance was driven by the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem, leading to record wireline orders that more than doubled year-over-year. Management attributed outperformance to increased test intensity as design margins shrink, requiring lossless performance that necessitates testing at the signal, bit, and protocol levels. The Commercial Communications segment achieved its first $1 billion quarter, with wireline revenue surpassing wireless for the first time due to AI-driven demand for 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers. Aerospace and defense growth was fueled by global deterrence needs and a shift toward advanced radar architectures and autonomous platforms like UAVs and LEO satellite constellations. Electronic Industrial Solutions saw record results driven by capacity expansion in advanced semiconductor nodes, high-bandwidth memory, and silicon photonics production. Strategic positioning with hyperscalers has deepened, moving beyond traditional CapEx into pre-silicon emulation and workload solutions integrated into customer development pipelines.

Outlook and Strategic Assumptions

Management expects Q4 orders to be slightly up from Q3 in line with seasonality, supported by a rolling 12-month funnel that currently stands at an all-time high. The 6G opportunity is projected to be larger than the 5G cycle, with the industry transitioning from exploratory research to funded development programs following the setting of a 2029 standard timeline. Supply chain constraints are expected to act as a 'governor' on near-term revenue conversion for the next several quarters due to high demand for incoming components across the ecosystem. Fiscal 2027 setup is characterized as strong, with management taking an 18-month-plus view on supply chain planning, including product redesigns to accommodate second-source components. Cost synergy realization from recent acquisitions is accelerating, with 80% to 90% of the $100 million target expected to be achieved on a run-rate basis exiting the fiscal year.

Operational Context and Risk Factors

Operating margins exceeded long-term targets, though management cautioned that one-time tariff impacts in FY26 will not repeat, creating a high comparison bar for future profitability. The mix of wireline business has shifted from a historical 80/20 R&D-to-manufacturing split to approximately 2/3 R&D and 1/3 manufacturing as AI data center build-outs scale. Integration of recent acquisitions, including Spirent, was completed one quarter ahead of schedule, enabling faster systems migration and synergy capture. Supply environment is currently less flexible than a year ago, requiring deeper engagement with suppliers to deconstrain production for high-demand new product introductions.

Sustainability of $2 billion quarterly order levels

Management expressed confidence in sustainability, citing the highest-ever monthly funnel intake in the most recent month and broad-based demand across all regions. Growth is being supported by nearly 3,000 new customers added year-to-date, representing over $100 million in incremental business.

title: Keysight Technologies Shares Rise After Record Third-Quarter Results
content:
Stock chart with green arrow moving up ©Adobe Stock Images

Keysight Technologies (NYSE:KEYS) shares climbed 2.6% in pre-market trading after the electronic design and testing specialist delivered record fiscal third-quarter results, comfortably exceeding Wall Street expectations for both earnings and revenue.

Adjusted earnings per share reached $3.07, well ahead of the analyst consensus of $2.48, while quarterly revenue came in at $1.85 billion versus expectations of $1.75 billion.

AI Infrastructure Demand Drives Orders Higher

Orders provided one of the strongest signals from the quarter, surging 56% year-on-year to $2.09 billion and significantly exceeding market expectations. Demand for testing solutions linked to artificial intelligence infrastructure was a major contributor to the increase.

Keysight's Communications Solutions Group emerged as the principal growth driver, with commercial communications revenue jumping 56%.

Within the division, the wireline business benefited substantially from accelerating AI data centre investment. For the first time in Keysight's history, wireline revenue surpassed revenue generated by the wireless business, highlighting the growing importance of AI-related infrastructure spending to the company's performance.

Keysight Guidance Comes In Well Above Wall Street Forecasts

The earnings beat was reinforced by a stronger-than-expected outlook for the fiscal fourth quarter.

Management forecast revenue of between $1.93 billion and $1.95 billion, comfortably above the analyst consensus of $1.82 billion.

Adjusted earnings per share are expected to range from $3.34 to $3.40, compared with Wall Street expectations of approximately $2.68 per share.

The substantial gap between Keysight's guidance and existing analyst forecasts provided investors with further evidence that strong demand could continue beyond the latest quarter.

Margins Expand as Free Cash Flow Reaches $403 Million

Keysight also demonstrated significant operating leverage during the period. Operating margin expanded by more than 800 basis points compared with the previous year, reflecting the benefits of stronger revenue and disciplined cost management.

Free cash flow reached $403 million, providing the company with additional financial flexibility while it continued to return capital through its share repurchase programme.

The combination of expanding margins and robust cash generation suggests Keysight is translating its strong demand environment into improved financial performance rather than relying solely on top-line growth.

AI Investment Supports Keysight's Growth Outlook

Story Continues

The broader market offered a modestly favourable backdrop, with S&P 500 futures gaining 0.1%, Dow Jones futures advancing 0.02% and Nasdaq futures rising 0.1% in pre-market trading.

Positive sentiment was also visible among companies exposed to testing, measurement and photonics, reflecting continued expectations for heavy capital expenditure by hyperscale technology companies building AI infrastructure.

For Keysight, the combination of a substantial earnings beat, 56% order growth and fourth-quarter guidance well above consensus strengthened the investment case around its exposure to the multi-year expansion of AI infrastructure.

That theme has already contributed to bullish analyst expectations for the stock, with several price targets sitting substantially above its current trading level, including a $400 target from Morgan Stanley.

 	* Meta Marshall, Morgan Stanley: asked about rising test intensity and incremental margin guardrails; Senior VP & President of Communications Solutions Group Kailash Narayanan said, "the design margins are shrinking," and "they also need to test it in production as well." (Senior VP & President Narayanan) Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty cautioned "we did have the onetime tariff impacts this year that kind of artificially pulled up '26 profitability that won't repeat." (Executive VP & CFO Dougherty)
 	* Mark Delaney, Goldman Sachs: asked if $2B-plus orders are sustainable and about supply; President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran said, "our base case is orders slightly up from Q3," while Senior Vice President of Global Sales Sung Yoon said, "we're confident in delivering another record quarter and surpassing $2 billion for the third consecutive quarter." (Senior Vice President Yoon) On supply, President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran said, "the supply environment is less flexible today than, let's say, a year ago." (President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran)
 	* Timothy Long, Barclays: asked about wireline mix shifting toward manufacturing and hyperscaler importance; Executive VP & CFO Dougherty said wireline shifted from "about 80-20" toward "more like 70-30" and recently "probably more like 2/3, 1/3." (Executive VP & CFO Dougherty) President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran said hyperscalers are "roughly 10% of our business" directly. (President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran)
 	* Matthew Niknam, Truist: questioned modest sequential Q4 revenue guide and asked for FY 2027 color; President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran said, "Supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue." (President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran) Executive VP & CFO Dougherty added, "demand is not the limiter" and said supply will be "a governor of our ability to convert demand into revenue for the next several quarters." (Executive VP & CFO Dougherty)

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

 	* Analysts’ tone was slightly negative to pressing on sustainability and constraints, with repeated probing on demand durability and fulfillment, including questions on whether demand is "sustainable" (Mark Delaney, Goldman Sachs) and whether "supply constraints" are limiting guidance (Matthew Niknam, Truist).
 	* Management’s tone was positive in prepared remarks and more guarded in Q&A around constraints, repeatedly returning to supply as a limiter, including "far exceeding our ability to supply" (President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran) and "a governor" (Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty).
 	* Versus the prior quarter, management shifted from describing supply management as having "no major concerns" (Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty, Q2) to emphasizing tighter conditions, including "the supply environment is less flexible today" (President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran).

QUARTER-OVER-QUARTER COMPARISON

 	* Management elevated AI infrastructure scaling as a key driver in both quarters, but Q3 added a notable mix change: "Wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time this quarter." (Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty)
 	* Q2 featured tariff-refund accounting effects; Q3 highlighted a non-repeating profitability tailwind: "we did have the onetime tariff impacts this year" that "won't repeat." (Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty)
 	* Q3 brought more explicit supply constraint language and near-term conversion limits, while Q2 emphasized strong demand without "pull-forwards" and described supply chain as actively managed with "no major concerns." (President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran; Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty, Q2)
 	* Analyst focus stayed concentrated on AI wireline, backlog/conversion, and margins, but Q3 showed increased emphasis on whether guidance is capped by supply and how much backlog may shift into the next fiscal year.

RISKS AND CONCERNS

 	* "The supply environment is less flexible today than, let's say, a year ago." (President, CEO & Director Satish Dhanasekaran) Management said mitigation includes working "with our suppliers to deconstrain the supply chain" and taking an "18-month-plus view of our supply chain planning." (President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran)
 	* "The only thing I would just caution people to pay attention to is we did have the onetime tariff impacts this year... that won't repeat." (Executive VP & CFO Neil Dougherty)
 	* "Supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue." (President, CEO & Director Dhanasekaran) "The supply situation is likely to be nonlinear." (Executive VP & CFO Dougherty)

FINAL TAKEAWAY

Keysight’s management described Q3 as a record quarter driven by AI infrastructure demand (particularly wireline), strength in aerospace/defense modernization, and broad-based EISG growth, while raising Q4 and full-year FY 2026 outlook. In Q&A, the dominant constraint shifted from demand visibility to supply-chain conversion, with executives repeatedly calling supply the near-term “governor” even as sales reported a growing pipeline and expectations to sustain $2B-plus orders into Q4.

title: Keysight Delivers New High-Performance 4x100GE Network Cybersecurity Test Platform
content:
Scalable 4x100GE test solution provides hyperscale traffic generation and cybersecurity validation in a compact 1 rack unit footprint

SANTA ROSA, Calif., July 09, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Keysight Technologies, Inc. (NYSE: KEYS) today announced the APS-ONE-400, a modular network cybersecurity test platform. This new 4x100GE platform significantly boosts performance for Layer 4-7 traffic, encrypted traffic, and Elephant Flow traffic all within a 1 rack unit (RU) system. It enables network equipment manufacturers (NEMs), service providers, and data center operators to validate demanding scenarios while lowering overall infrastructure requirements.

The growing complexity and volume of network loads — including legitimate and malicious traffic, post-quantum cryptography (PQC)-encrypted traffic, Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), and the Elephant Flow transmissions common in AI and large language model (LLM) workloads — require network equipment manufacturers (NEMs), service providers, and data center operators to validate that their solutions can withstand these demands prior to deployment. However, this often requires multiple specialized test tools that can drive up costs and consume limited lab resources.

To address this challenge, Keysight developed the APS-ONE-400 appliance, an addition to its APS-100/400GE hardware family. The new modular, scalable 4x100GE network application and cybersecurity test platform generates hyperscale Layer 4-7 traffic, PQC-encrypted Transport Layer Security (TLS) throughput, security strikes, and ZTNA test capabilities — all within a compact 1RU footprint that improves lab efficiency.

The APS-ONE-400 4x100GE test platform offers the following benefits:

Increased performance and efficiency: Delivers 400 gigabits per second (Gbps) Layer 4-7 throughput, 380 Gbps of hardware-accelerated encrypted TLS throughput, 95 Gbps Elephant Flow throughput, and the latest security strikes in a compact 1RU platform that minimizes rack space, cooling, and power consumption. Compatibility and flexibility: Deploy as a stand-alone appliance or seamlessly integrate with existing deployments of Keysight's APS-100/400GE series, including APS-M8400, APS-M1010, and APS-ONE-100. With APS-ONE-400's fanout support for 100/25/10GE, the platform accommodates a range of critical network speeds. Hyperscale performance: When paired with the APS-M8400 appliance or APS-M1010 management controller, the APS-ONE-400 enables hyperscale testbeds that emulate the rigorous demands of data center and service provider environments. The platform can generate up to 16 terabits per second (Tbps) of Layer 4-7 traffic, 20 billion concurrent connections, 15 Tbps of TLS traffic, and 25 million TLS connections per second. Modular, scalable solution: Designed as a "pay-as-you-grow" solution, the APS-ONE-400 lets users support current test needs while retaining the flexibility to scale up capacity as requirements evolve.

Story Continues

Ram Periakaruppan, Vice President and General Manager, Keysight's Network Test and Security Solutions, said: "The exponential growth of data transfers and bandwidth demands generated by AI and machine learning workloads is putting unprecedented strain on data center, service provider, and enterprise network infrastructures. Continuously validating that networks can handle these challenges without compromising security requires realistic, hyperscale, traffic emulation capabilities. Keysight's modular APS-ONE-400 compute node delivers new heights in realism, emulating the traffic flows associated with generative AI models and agentic applications at hyperscale, including the huge Elephant Flow datasets common to LLM training use cases and PQC-encrypted traffic flows, all in a compact form factor that conserves critical lab resources."

Resources

Product Page:APS-100/400 network security test platform Data Sheet:APS-100/400 network security test platform

About Keysight Technologies

At Keysight (NYSE: KEYS), we inspire and empower innovators to bring world-changing technologies to life. As an S&P 500 company, we're delivering market-leading design, emulation, and test solutions to help engineers develop and deploy faster, with less risk, throughout the entire product lifecycle. We're a global innovation partner enabling customers in communications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, automotive, semiconductor, and general electronics markets to accelerate innovation to connect and secure the world. Learn more at Keysight Newsroom and www.keysight.com.

The Keysight APS-ONE-400 4x100GE modular network cybersecurity test platform delivers hyperscale L4-7 traffic, encrypted TLS traffic, security strikes, and Elephant Flows via a 1RU footprint that minimizes rack space usage, power consumption, and cooling demands.

title: Keysight Technologies, Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary
content:
Keysight Technologies, Inc. Q1 2026 Earnings Call Summary - Moby

Strategic Performance Drivers

Performance was driven by the convergence of AI-driven technology transformations, next-generation connectivity, and rising semiconductor complexity. Wireline orders reached record levels, surpassing wireless for the first time, as hyperscalers scale-up and scale-out AI infrastructure architectures. The shift toward Ethernet-based AI fabrics and 800G/1.6T optics is creating high-intensity validation requirements across the entire infrastructure stack. Aerospace and Defense growth reached record Q1 levels due to global focus on deterrence and U.S. prime contractors ramping radar production and organic R&D. Electronic Industrial growth was fueled by high-bandwidth memory expansion and increasing complexity in high-performance PCB manufacturing. Management attributes the current inflection to three years of strategic investments in a 'full stack' portfolio that enables end-to-end validation from design to deployment. The company is successfully broadening its customer base beyond traditional silicon providers to include neoclouds and international manufacturing ecosystems.

Outlook and Strategic Assumptions

Fiscal 2026 annual revenue and earnings growth expectations have been raised to just above 20% based on current visibility and funnel strength. Management anticipates sustained demand from concurrent technology waves, where 800G ramping overlaps with accelerated 1.6T and 3.2T R&D cycles. The 6G commercialization timeline remains targeted for 2030, with large-scale technology demonstrations expected at the 2028 L.A. Olympics. Guidance assumes continued strength in European defense budgets driven by regional sovereignty priorities and national security needs. Acquisition revenue for fiscal 2026 is projected at $375 million, with cost synergies heavily weighted toward late 2026 following ERP migration.

Operational Context and Risks

The Q2 2026 guidance does not include potential impacts from a recent Supreme Court decision regarding tariffs, which the company is currently assessing. Recent acquisitions (Spirent, Optical Design, PowerArtist) are currently dilutive to operating margins but are expected to be accretive following $100 million in synergies. The Board has authorized a $1.5 billion stock buyback program as part of its capital allocation strategy. Supply chain management has factored in rising memory prices, though the company notes it does not have high-volume usage of specialized AI DRAM.

title: Keysight signals 30% Q2 revenue growth and 35% EPS rise, highlights robust AI and defense demand
content:
Earnings Call Insights: Keysight Technologies (KEYS) Q1 2026

MANAGEMENT VIEW

 	* Satish Dhanasekaran, President and CEO, stated that "Keysight delivered outstanding results with both revenue and earnings per share exceeding the high end of our guidance range," crediting robust growth across business segments and regions. He cited AI-driven technology transformations, next-generation connectivity, rising semiconductor complexity, and defense modernization as primary secular tailwinds. 
 	* Dhanasekaran highlighted that in the Communication Solutions segment, "order growth outpaced revenue growth of 27% in the quarter," with wireline delivering record orders, surpassing wireless for the first time. He noted, "AI infrastructure is rapidly scaling... Hyperscalers and their respective ecosystems are investing in designing and deploying scale-up and scale-out architectures."
 	* The company reported record orders in aerospace, defense, and government (ADG) with growth across all regions, driven by "heightened global focus on deterrence and defense modernization priorities."
 	* The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group achieved record revenue, with double-digit growth in general electronics, semiconductors, and automotive and energy. Dhanasekaran said, "Orders grew for the third consecutive quarter, and revenue was a record."
 	* Neil Dougherty, Executive VP & CFO, reported, "First quarter total company revenue of $1.600 billion was up 23% on a reported basis," and "orders of $1.645 billion were up 30% on a reported basis." He added, "Gross margin was 66.7%, up 90 basis points, driven by favorable product mix."
 	* Dougherty also stated, "We delivered net income of $376 million and earnings per share of $2.17, both up 19%."

OUTLOOK

 	* Dougherty provided guidance for Q2 2026: "We expect revenue in the range of $1.690 billion to $1.710 billion, representing 30% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. We expect Q2 earnings per share to be in the range of $2.27 to $2.33, representing 35% year-over-year growth at the midpoint."
 	* The expectation for $375 million in acquisition-related revenue for fiscal '26 remains unchanged, as does the synergy target of more than $100 million in run rate cost synergies, "with realization heavily weighted to late in 2026."
 	* Dougherty noted, "With the visibility we currently have, our base case for fiscal '26 has increased as we now expect total annual revenue and earnings growth just above 20%."

FINANCIAL RESULTS

 	* Keysight reported total company revenue of $1.600 billion, up 23% on a reported basis.
 	* Orders reached $1.645 billion, up 30%.
 	* Gross margin was 66.7%, and operating margin reached 27.4%.
 	* Net income was $376 million, with earnings per share of $2.17, both rising 19%.
 	* Communications Solutions Group revenue was $1.124 billion, up 27%.
 	* Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $476 million, up 15%.
 	* Software and services represented approximately 40% of Keysight revenue, while annual recurring revenue was 29% of total mix.
 	* Cash flow from operations was $441 million, with free cash flow of $407 million. The company repurchased approximately 420,000 shares for total consideration of $87 million.

Q&A

 	* Aaron Rakers, Wells Fargo: Asked about AI-driven growth, especially wireline surpassing wireless. Dhanasekaran responded, "We sized our AI exposure last year in Q4 to be just about 10% of the company revenue. And on that run rate, we had robust order growth and significantly above company average."
 	* Rakers followed up on operating leverage. Dougherty said, "We've designed our business model about delivering 40% core leverage on growth that's in the mid-single digits or better."
 	* Meta Marshall, Morgan Stanley: Inquired about AI customer base broadening. Dhanasekaran noted, "We've doubled the number of customers that represented that demand."
 	* Mark Delaney, Goldman Sachs: Questioned second-half expectations. Dougherty explained, "We have really strong visibility 1 quarter out, pretty decent visibility 2 quarters out, and then it falls off beyond that."
 	* Andrew Spinola, UBS: Asked about competitive landscape in AI. Dhanasekaran stated, "Keysight's competitive advantage is that we are designed to be a solutions-oriented company."

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

 	* Analysts showed a positive to slightly positive tone, focusing on AI growth, customer base expansion, and strong order momentum, while some sought clarity on potential supply chain constraints and guidance assumptions.
 	* Management maintained a confident and upbeat tone throughout, especially in prepared remarks. During Q&A, management used phrases such as "we feel good about our ability to execute" and "we have confidence in our ability to outperform."
 	* Compared to last quarter, both analysts and management exhibited higher confidence, with multiple references to "momentum" and "robust pipelines."

QUARTER-OVER-QUARTER COMPARISON

 	* Q1 2026 guidance for revenue and EPS is significantly higher than Q4 2025, with management now projecting total annual revenue and earnings growth just above 20%, compared to the previous quarter's expectation for growth "at or above the high end of our 5% to 7% long-term target."
 	* Strategic focus shifted toward more explicit expansion in AI and defense, while highlighting record wireline and ADG orders.
 	* Analysts' questions in the current quarter focused more on AI-driven demand, competitive differentiation, and customer base broadening, reflecting increased attention to secular technology trends.
 	* Management's tone is notably more confident, reinforcing growth prospects and highlighting order momentum and pipeline strength.

RISKS AND CONCERNS

 	* Dougherty stated that Q2 guidance "does not contemplate any impact from the recently announced Supreme Court decision regarding tariffs," and the company is still assessing effects.
 	* Memory price increases were noted, but management reported these have already been factored into outlook and guidance.
 	* Management acknowledged ongoing integration of acquisitions and the need to execute on synergy targets and ERP migration for full benefits realization.

FINAL TAKEAWAY

Keysight Technologies began fiscal 2026 with robust growth across all business segments, supported by accelerating AI infrastructure investment, expanding defense budgets, and strong demand for next-generation connectivity and semiconductor solutions. Management raised its full-year outlook, signaling confidence in sustained double-digit growth and operational leverage, while emphasizing strategic positioning to capture emerging opportunities in AI, defense, and industrial markets. The company remains focused on executing its integration and synergy plans, monitoring tariff-related risks, and maintaining strong cash flow to support both organic and inorganic growth initiatives.

title: Keysight expects FY 2026 revenue growth at or above 7% target while expanding AI and 6G initiatives
content:
Earnings Call Insights: Keysight Technologies (KEYS) Q4 2025

MANAGEMENT VIEW

 	* Satish Dhanasekaran, President and CEO, reported "Keysight delivered an outstanding fourth quarter results exceeding the high end of our guidance. Orders grew 14%, revenue increased 10% and EPS rose 16%." He described full year orders and revenue growth of 8% and EPS up 14%, noting, "Keysight's leadership and differentiated solutions continue to drive demand across our markets." 
 	* Dhanasekaran highlighted the company's portfolio is "enabling major innovation waves shaping our markets, AI and accelerated compute, nonterrestrial networks, 6G, next-gen semiconductors and defense modernization." He pointed to acquisitions of Spirent, Synopsys Optical Solutions Group and Ansys Power Artist as advancing Keysight's software-centric strategy.
 	* He announced, "our Board has authorized an additional $1.5 billion share repurchase program supporting our ongoing capital return."
 	* Dhanasekaran stated, "Wireline orders and revenue grew double digits both in Q4 and for the full year, setting a new record for the business," and described AI infrastructure build-outs as a key driver. He also noted, "Wireless orders and revenue grew high single digits for the full year and outperformed expectations, driven by ongoing standards evolutions, nonterrestrial networks and early 6G research."
 	* Neil Dougherty, Executive VP & CFO, said, "Fourth quarter revenue of $1.419 billion was above the high end of our guidance range, up 10% on a reported basis or 9% on a core basis. Orders of $1.533 billion were up 14% on a reported basis or 12% on a core basis." Dougherty added, "We generated $331 million of net income and delivered earnings per share of $1.91, which increased 16% year-over-year."

OUTLOOK

 	* Dougherty stated, "For the first quarter of 2026, we expect revenue in the range of $1.530 billion to $1.550 billion, representing 19% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Excluding the recent acquisitions, this guidance assumes 10% year-over-year revenue growth."
 	* For the full year, he said, "we expect FY '26 revenue growth, excluding acquisitions, to be at or above the high end of our 5% to 7% long-term target."
 	* He noted acquisitions are expected to contribute approximately $375 million of revenue in FY '26 and "we are working to realize in excess of $100 million of synergies and other operational efficiencies across Keysight."
 	* Dougherty indicated the acquisitions "are expected to be accretive to Keysight's earnings 12 months post close. While this implies some mild dilution in FY '26, we expect the strength of our core business to enable FY '26 EPS growth at or above our long-term 10% target."

FINANCIAL RESULTS

 	* Dougherty reported, "For the full year, Keysight generated revenue of $5.375 billion, up 8% as reported or 7% on a core basis. Gross margin was 65% and operating margin was 26%. FY '25 earnings per share of $7.16 was up 14%."
 	* Communications Solutions Group (CSG) revenue was $990 million, up 11%. Commercial Communications revenue reached $660 million, up 12%. Aerospace, defense and government revenue was $330 million, up 9%.
 	* Electronic Industrial Solutions Group (EISG) revenue was $429 million, up 9%.
 	* Software and services accounted for approximately 37% of revenue, with annual recurring revenue at 29% of total.
 	* The company ended the quarter with $1.9 billion in cash and cash equivalents, generating $225 million in cash flow from operations and $188 million in free cash flow; $1.7 billion was deployed for acquisitions.

Q&A

 	* Mehdi Hosseini, Susquehanna Financial Group: Asked about wireless trends. Dhanasekaran responded, "wireless exceeded expectations this year, in part driven by stabilization in 5G, which is normalized and then some of the advanced technology areas that we have made investments in starting to show some early results even prior to 6G hitting inflection."
 	* Samik Chatterjee, JPMorgan: Inquired about order acceleration and drivers. Dhanasekaran replied, "the revenue outperformance was driven by the broad order strength that we saw with both our CSG and EISG businesses growing double digits this quarter," and added, "the volume of the pipeline or the velocity of the pipeline or the conversion rate... they're all trending up."
 	* Andrew Spinola, UBS: Asked about wireline business timing and hyperscaler impact. Dhanasekaran indicated, "the AI cluster and infrastructure build-outs are occurring, driven by the hyperscaler spend."
 	* Atif Malik, Citi: Questioned 6G adoption timeline with new AI partnerships. Dhanasekaran stated, "we're thinking '28, '29-ish time frame when that process comes to some level of maturity before global deployments may occur."
 	* Robert Mason, Baird: Asked about positioning capabilities from Spirent acquisition. Dhanasekaran called positioning "a crown jewel... very unique capabilities with regard to positioning, navigation and time."
 	* David Ridley-Lane, BofA Securities: Asked about EPS dilution. Dougherty replied, "I described it in the prepared remarks as mild. So I think you could think of it on a percentage basis is low single digits."
 	* Mark Delaney, Goldman Sachs: Inquired about growth by business line and tariffs. Dougherty explained, "wireline, we're clearly benefiting from the investment wave in AI" and added, "our pricing and surcharging mitigations are ramping a little faster than expected."
 	* Aaron Rakers, Wells Fargo: Asked about operating margin targets. Dougherty stated, "it's further out" for reaching 31%-32% operating margin, citing the recent downturn.
 	* Meta Marshall, Morgan Stanley: Asked about strength in Aerospace and Defense and automotive. Dhanasekaran said, "record bookings this year builds backlog again."
 	* Tim Long, Barclays: Asked about AI and software/services growth. Dhanasekaran noted, "our wireline business had a record year, growing double digits this year," and software and services are expected to reach 40% with M&A.
 	* Rob Jamieson, Vertical Research Partners: Inquired about R&D investment. Dhanasekaran said, "we're in between that refresh phase of investment right now and over the next 18 months, feel really good about the new product introductions."

SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

 	* Analyst sentiment showed cautious optimism, pressing for specifics on wireless, AI, synergy realization, and margin expansion. Questions focused on growth sustainability and acquisition integration.
 	* Management maintained a confident and positive tone, using language such as "we feel good about this, and we reflected that in our guide," and "we are confident in the fundamentals of our business model." There was no sign of defensiveness or hesitation in responses.
 	* Compared to the previous quarter, both analyst and management tone remained positive but showed more confidence due to accelerated growth and strong order momentum.

QUARTER-OVER-QUARTER COMPARISON

 	* Guidance language shifted from "gradual recovery" in Q3 to more robust expectations, with FY '26 revenue growth forecast at or above the high end of the 5%-7% target.
 	* Strategic focus expanded with three acquisitions completed, adding software-centric capabilities.
 	* Analyst questions this quarter focused more on AI-driven growth, acquisition integration, and cadence of M&A contributions, versus last quarter's tariff mitigation and order visibility.
 	* Management confidence increased, with Dhanasekaran and Dougherty citing strong pipelines and robust order growth, compared to a more cautious optimism in Q3.
 	* Key metrics such as EPS, revenue, and order growth all improved quarter-over-quarter.

RISKS AND CONCERNS

 	* Management identified ongoing geopolitical and policy uncertainties.
 	* Dougherty mentioned "mild dilution in FY '26" from acquisitions, expecting it to be offset by core business strength.
 	* Tariff impacts remain a focus, but mitigation strategies are proceeding ahead of schedule.
 	* Analysts pressed on the sustainability of growth, integration of acquisitions, and timing of synergy realization.

FINAL TAKEAWAY

Keysight Technologies closes fiscal 2025 with strong momentum, highlighted by double-digit order and revenue growth in Q4, robust contributions from AI and 6G, and successful integration of new acquisitions. Management signals confidence in further accelerating revenue and EPS growth for FY 2026, supported by a healthy pipeline, expanding software and services portfolio, and proactive capital return strategies, while closely monitoring geopolitical and integration risks.
